title: Working for Lady Day: Pepe and how she asked for him
summary: He loved working with Billie Holiday and recalls what her lawyer said.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: When I used to work for Lady Day, it was like... I was a lot younger, you know, of course... It was like I couldn't wait to get there. I just couldn't wait to get there and see her and Pepe, her little dog. I'd go all the way up to his ears, and then he'd start snapping his teeth and I'd quit. Because he'd turn around and bite your hand if you went past his ears.
What kind of a dog was that? That wasn't the little boxer she had.
He was a Mexican Hairless or some damn thing. He was a little piece of shit that you could stick in a pinhole. But he was Pepe!

I was lucky, I think. I wasn't working with her when she was all strung out and all ...[VOLUME BRIEFLY DROPS DRAMATICALLY, TO INAUDIBILITY]... I was lucky. I worked for her when she was in California. I never travelled with her. But it's probably better. And the lawyer... Last night we met Earl, he was her lawyer for the last three years. And

he told me that she used to ask about me, talk about me. She said, 'I wish I had him, but I can't afford him.' And that just stopped me, that she would remember... 'I wish I had him, but I can't afford him.' But every time I'd come to California to record, BANG... And I was on all those records. Unless I was doing something else; they used Oscar.
You did all those nice things with Ben and Benny Carter and Sweets...

Yeah. Norman would never give me much of a chance. He had too many big stars there. I was just there. She wanted me there. That's all. As long as I was sitting at the piano, she was happy. She didn't give a shit whether I played a solo or what. I loved her.
